name: Baker House
description: A six-story MIT dormitory on the Charles River, built as an undulating slab clad in rough brick. Over 90 percent of the student rooms look out onto the river. It has a two-story limestone-clad dining pavilion with a bank of circular skylights, and a great stucco-clad stair hangs on the north facade.
significance_text: Docomomo US describes it as a pivotal building in Alvar Aalto's career, the most significant of his works in North America, and the first major building to synthesize European Modernism with the regional material vernacular of New England. It was Aalto's second building constructed in the United States, designed during his time teaching at MIT.

admission.notes: A private university residence hall. No public interior tours or visiting hours were found. Guests must be escorted by a resident host. View the building from Memorial Drive and the riverside.
